hypotheses.justification: This follows from the other instances. `ℚ_[p]` has characteristic zero and `algebraMap ℚ_[p] K` is injective (it is a ring hom out of a field into a nontrivial ring), so `charZero_of_injective_algebraMap` (Mathlib/Algebra/CharP/Algebra.lean) gives `CharZero K` from `[Algebra ℚ_[p] K]`. The same lemma also gives it from `[CharZero L]` together with the injective map `algebraMap K L`. The degenerate cases do not arise: both are fields, so they are nontrivial. New proof: `haveI : CharZero K := charZero_of_injective_algebraMap (algebraMap ℚ_[p] K).injective`, then the original term `(groupCohomology_res_padicCompletionUnits p K L S).2`. The statement itself does not change.

This also follows from the other instances. `charZero_of_injective_algebraMap` applied to the injective `algebraMap ℚ_[p] L` gives `CharZero L` from `[Algebra ℚ_[p] L]`, since `ℚ_[p]` has characteristic zero. It also follows from `[CharZero K]` through the injective `algebraMap K L`. New proof: `haveI : CharZero L := charZero_of_injective_algebraMap (algebraMap ℚ_[p] L).injective`, then the existing proof. Because the derivation goes through `ℚ_[p]`, `[CharZero K]` and `[CharZero L]` can even be deleted together.

`FiniteDimensional K L` is by definition `Module.Finite K L`. It follows from `[Module.Finite ℚ_[p] L]` and `[IsScalarTower ℚ_[p] K L]` (with `[Algebra ℚ_[p] K]`, which supplies the `SMul ℚ_[p] K`) by `Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite ℚ_[p] K L` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Basic.lean). New proof: `haveI : FiniteDimensional K L := Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite ℚ_[p] K L`, then the original proof `(groupCohomology_res_padicCompletionUnits p K L S).2`.
